ingredients.item: Chili oil (check the label for nuts)

instructions: Put the chicken in a medium pot with the ginger slices and the 2 scallion lengths. Cover with about 2 inches of cold water and set it on high heat.

Bring it to a boil, then cover, turn off the heat, and leave the chicken for 25 minutes. You're cooking it to 165°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest piece: it's done when there's no pink left.
Meanwhile, fill a large pot with water and bring it to a boil for the noodles.
Mince the 6 garlic cloves. In a large bowl, stir together the garlic, rice vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar and salt until the sugar dissolves.
Cut the cucumber into matchsticks, chop the cilantro and finely chop the 2 remaining scallions.
Boil the noodles for the time on the package. Drain them, rinse well with cold water, and drain again.
Transfer the chicken to a cutting board and shred it into thin strips with two forks or your fingers.
Add the noodles, chicken, cucumber, bean sprouts, chopped scallions and cilantro to the bowl with the sauce. Toss until everything is coated.
Serve cold with the chili oil on the side for the adults.
method_notes: The Woks of Life (4.87 from 22) leads: poached chicken, cold noodles, cucumber and sprouts under a soy, vinegar and garlic sauce. The recipe is doubled from two servings to four, the garlic is cut from 8 cloves to 6 for a milder base, and the chili oil moves to the table. The peanuts it calls for are left out to keep it nut-free. The honest total is 40 minutes because the chicken rests for 25, but only about 15 of those are hands on, and the finished dish packs cold.
